checks.description: rate[dna02, leg_mn_right] / rate[dna01] > 1.0  [0/3 seeds, sd 13.9]  [floored: every compared condition silent]
checks.basis: Rayshubskiy et al. 2025: rotational velocity is a steep function of DNa02 activity and a shallow one of DNa01 activity — equal drive should move the motor pool more (inferred to MN rate); > 1 is the task-18 convention for a direction

checks.description: rate[dna02, leg_mn_right] / rate[dna02, leg_mn_left] > 1.0  [0/3 seeds, sd 36.2]  [floored: every compared condition silent]
checks.basis: Rayshubskiy et al. 2025: unilateral DNa02 activation gives an ipsilateral steering bias, and every direct DNa02 -> MN synapse in MaleCNS is ipsilateral (490 right, 0 left): the right pool must move more than the left (inferred to MN rate); > 1 is the task-18 direction convention

null check. Rayshubskiy et al. 2025: steering commands are see-saw — excitation of one DNa02 with inhibition of the contralateral copy; the right DNa02 makes no synapse on the left one (inferred: the twin must not be co-activated); 2 Hz is the task-05 convention for silence

tasks.title: The compass keeps one bump, keeps it in the dark, and picks one of two cues

checks.basis: Seelig & Jayaraman 2015; Kim et al. 2017: a single bump of ~90° FWHM (population-vector length ~0.85 for such a bump; 0.5 is the length of a bump half the ring wide — convention)

checks.description: bump error[cue, vs 135°] < 45.0 deg  [3/3 seeds, sd 0]
checks.basis: Seelig & Jayaraman 2015: the bump sits at the cue's heading; 45° is one wedge of the eight-wedge readout (convention)
Seelig & Jayaraman 2015: the bump persists after the visual cue is removed; 5 Hz over the whole ring is the task-02 convention for a response

checks.description: bump resultant[cue, 8 wedges] > 0.5  [0/3 seeds, sd nan]
checks.basis: Seelig & Jayaraman 2015; Kim et al. 2017: one bump persists in darkness (the attractor); 0.5 convention as above

checks.description: bump error[cue, vs 135°] < 45.0 deg  [0/3 seeds, sd nan]
checks.basis: Seelig & Jayaraman 2015: drift in darkness is slow (tens of degrees over seconds); under 45° in the 0.7 s after cue offset (convention)
Kim et al. 2017: two competing cues do not produce two bumps, one wins (winner-take-all); two equal opposite bumps give a population-vector length of 0
